scores.rationale: Declaration, request digest, public run order, output bytes, API bytes and all integer joins pass deterministic replay.
Both outputs preserve public-account non-authority and explicitly avoid guaranteed protection or execution claims.
Both lanes choose the allowed read-only hold decision and record no wallet, signature, repayment or broadcast.
All three observation numerators, denominators and floor-scaled 18-decimal health factors recompute from the frozen request.
The minimum health factor, 144-second window, thresholds and no-trigger latency state match the frozen policy.

verification.method: Recomputed raw receipt digests and schemas; reobserved three exact public blocks, dual-provider testnet run order, and public hire receipt. Validated retained historical Health Guardian A2A bytes without reinvocation.
verification.verifier: ProofEra owner-designated internal TermiX reviewer A

limitations: The manual no-agent statement and source provenance still require a genuinely independent second reviewer.
Zero incremental onchain cost excludes human labor and the earlier marketplace hire; no currency conversion is performed.
Public-account observations grant no ProofEra authority and prove no autonomous intervention or guaranteed protection.
The score applies only to three retained observations and the frozen threshold policy.
Owner-designated internal review; not an external or cryptographically authenticated reviewer identity.
No Sigstore attestation; this review is not transaction, signing, broadcast, or custody authorization.
No future runtime envelope was reviewed or authorized; materialization and final compilation must still fail closed on the exact clean published release.
Historical A2A endpoints were not reinvoked; retained raw bytes were digest, schema, and output-core checked, while public immutable receipts and state were reobserved read-only.
The manual no-agent conclusion is bounded to committed runner and import boundaries, invocation declarations, and retained tool logs; it is not cryptographic proof of tools outside the packet.
Future archive or RPC provider availability is not guaranteed; missing future evidence cannot become a verified claim.
